title: Lean-Verified Proof Establishes Impossibility & Query Cost of Simulating the Quantum Switch
aiSystem: GPT, Claude & Gemini Frontier Models + Lean 4 (Yale)
whyItMatters: Machine-checked in Lean 4 with AI models working out most technical details, this proof settles Bavaresco et al.’s quantum-causality conjecture: no finite causally ordered quantum circuit can exactly simulate the quantum switch.
summary: Posted to arXiv on November 12, 2026 (arXiv:2611.16229) by Dantong Li at Yale University, with frontier GPT, Claude, and Gemini models explicitly credited with working out most technical proof details and writing the Lean 4 formalization, this paper settles the conjecture of Bavaresco et al. on indefinite causal order. It proves that no causally ordered quantum circuit using any finite number of black-box calls can exactly simulate the quantum switch—which applies quantum operations in a coherent superposition of causal orders—establishes a polynomial query lower bound of Ω(d^{1/4}) (with diamond-norm bounds scaling in dimension d) for approximate simulation, and demonstrates an exponential query advantage of the quantum switch over ordinary circuits on a practical quantum error-correction noise-discrimination task.
technicalHighlights: Settled Bavaresco et al.’s conjecture by proving exact simulation of the quantum switch with finitely many causally ordered circuit queries is mathematically impossible.
Established quantitative approximate simulation query lower bounds scaling with Hilbert-space dimension d and an exponential separation on channel noise characterization.
Accompanied by a machine-checked Lean 4 formalization produced primarily by collaborating frontier GPT, Claude, and Gemini models.
caveats: Recent November 2026 arXiv preprint; while the core proof is formalized in Lean 4, independent peer review of the physical/quantum-information exposition and statement alignment is ongoing.

scoreRationale.foundational: Resolves a central theoretical question on the computational power of indefinite causal order in quantum mechanics.
scoreRationale.ripple: Clarifies provable query-complexity separations relevant to quantum metrology, channel discrimination, and quantum error-correction noise diagnostics.
scoreRationale.verification: Core impossibility and query-complexity theorems are machine-checked in Lean 4, awaiting journal peer review.
scoreRationale.velocity: Multi-model AI reasoning and automated Lean 4 formalization compressed intricate supermap/diamond-norm proof engineering.
